questions.question: A researcher wants to test whether a new teaching method improves student performance. 27 students take a math test before and after the new method is implemented. The researcher records their scores / [CO4] before and after the intervention. Use Sign test at 5% level of significance to check whether there is a statistically significant difference in student performance after using the new teaching method? Students Test Scores(Before and After) Before: 70, 68, 85, 90,76, 82, 65, 76, 74, 88, 86,78,76, 89, 90, 85, 84, 83, 70, 73, 77, 87,67, 90, 85, 72, 72 After : 75, 72, 84, 91, 80, 83, 70, 78, 77, 75, 78, 89, 69, 80, 91, 87, 83, 85, 79, 76, 79, 85, 64,91,90,69, 68 [12x1 = 12]
questions.solution_html:
• Either sign test or Wilcoxon signed rank test
  • A) Sign Test
  • Compute the difference for each student:
  • 5, 4, −1, 1, 4, 1, 5, 2, 3, −13, −8, 11, −7, −9, 1, 2, −1, 2, 9, 3, 2, −2, −3, 1, 5, −3, −4 2 marks
  • No. of positive differences -17, No.of negative differences : 10, Number of ties: 0; n = 27
  • - 4 marks
  • test statistic- X- no.of positive values 2 marks
  • 𝐻0 : (no median change)
  • X∼Binomial(27,0.5)
  • Two-sided exact p-value = 0.2478. 3 marks
  • Conclusion (α = 0.05): fail to reject 𝐻0 . No statistically significant change. 1 mark
  • .
  • B) Wilcoxon signed-rank test (paired, uses magnitudes + signs)
  • • Absolute differences were ranked 5 marks
  • • Sum of ranks for positive differences W+=221.5 2mark
  • • For n=27 the normal-approximation with continuity correction gives
  • z ≈ 0.769 and two-sided p-value ≈ 0.4420. 4 mark
  • Conclusion (α = 0.05): fail to reject null hypothesis . No statistically significant change. 1 mark
